summary: Mantius (Ancient Greek Μαντίος, "diviner, seer") was a son of the Argive seer Melampus and Iphianassa, brother of Antiphates, and father of Cleitus and Polypheides — whom Apollo made the greatest mortal seer after Amphiaraus. Some versions also name him father of Oicles.
etymology: Ancient Greek Μαντίος (Mantíos), from μάντις "seer, prophet."

sections.heading: Melampodid line
paragraphs: In the Odyssey Melampus' son Mantius fathers Cleitus — whom Dawn snatches for his beauty — and Polypheides, whom Apollo sets as chief seer among mortals once Amphiaraus is dead. Apollodorus keeps Mantius in the same Melampodid stem at Argos.
Pausanias preserves related Melampodid local lore; the name itself advertises the family's mantic vocation.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: Mantius is also a genus of jumping spiders — irrelevant to the mythic node. The atlas id mantius-melampid is Melampus' Argive son alone.
